title: Ex 2.6 #7 · P ⇒ Q = (P ∧ ∼Q) ⇒ (Q ∧ ∼Q)
prompt: Use a truth table to show that $P \Rightarrow Q$ and $(P \wedge \sim Q) \Rightarrow (Q \wedge \sim Q)$ are logically equivalent: they have the same truth value in every row.
answer_format: No final answer box. Give the truth-table column of each statement as a column step (statement : T F T T, rows (P, Q) in the order TT, TF, FT, FF), or rewrite one statement into the other with expr steps, each equivalent to the one before.
hints: Q ∧ ∼Q is false in every row, so the right side is an implication with a false conclusion.
An implication with a false conclusion is true exactly when its hypothesis is false.
solution: $\sim Q$ is F T F T, so $P \wedge \sim Q$ is F T F F, and $Q \wedge \sim Q$ is F F F F.
So $(P \wedge \sim Q) \Rightarrow (Q \wedge \sim Q)$ is T F T T: it is false only in the row where $P \wedge \sim Q$ is true.
$P \Rightarrow Q$ is also T F T T, so the statements are logically equivalent.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses logical equivalence (Section 2.6).
